title: Allocation stewardship and downloads playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for how we present cost allocation ownership, who can download which invoice/export, and how budgets & alerts surface in downloads. Focus is on practical UX decisions (visibility, defaults, filters) and a prioritized grooming backlog to get a minimum viable export flow shipped that satisfies Compliance + Billing customers.

Problem statement:
- Customers need clear ownership and an auditable trail for cost exports (finance, platform, product teams).
- Exports are frequently requested by internal stakeholders and external auditors; current console flow is confusing (multiple places to download, inconsistent columns, unclear account scoping).
- Budgets and alerts currently live in separate UI from exports; customers expect the exported CSV/JSON to include budget attribution and alert state.

Goals (explicit):
1) One canonical export flow for invoices/cost-allocation that supports: date ranges, cost centers/tags, cost allocation rules, budgets, and alert annotations.
2) Role-based visibility: finance sees everything; owners see their cost centers; read-only viewers can request exports.
3) Exports include metadata for traceability: requestor, export timestamp, schema version, linked budget IDs, and a short change log.
4) UX minimalism for common tasks: default to last_invoice / last_30_days, single-click CSV download for small ranges, async export for large ranges with email/console notification.

User personas & key stories (prioritized):
- Finance Analyst (primary): "I need a consolidated monthly CSV with cost center breakdown and budget variance for the month end audit."
- Platform PM (secondary): "I want a per-model cost report to forward to infra for optimization."
- Team Lead (tertiary): "I want a one-click export of my team's charges and any alerts triggered this quarter."
- Auditor (external): "I need a signed export with requestor and export hash for verification."

Wireframe notes (screens + states):
1) Exports launcher (top-right of Billing Overview)
   - Single entrypoint labeled "Export & Downloads". Small helper text: "Download charges, allocation, budgets, and alerts."
   - CTA opens modal with 3 tabs: Quick Export, Custom Export, Export History.

2) Quick Export
   - Preset date ranges: Last invoice (default), Last 30 days, Last 90 days, Custom range
   - Scope dropdown: All org / Cost center / Tag set / Model name
   - Output format: CSV (default) | JSON | Parquet (advanced)
   - Checkboxes: Include budgets? Include alerts? Include allocation rules?
   - Quick note: "CSV limited to 50k rows; larger exports are processed as async and emailed."

3) Custom Export
   - Column picker (multi-select) with recommended defaults: date, cost_center, charge_amount, allocation_rule, budget_id, budget_state, alert_ids, requestor, export_id
   - Advanced filters: exclude credits/refunds, group by cost_center or tag, aggregation level (daily/monthly)
   - Delivery options: Download now (sync) / Queue export (async + email) / S3 delivery (enterprise)

4) Export History
   - List of past exports with status, requested by, scope, row_count, and a download link for completed items
   - Actions: Re-run export, Share link (time-limited), Revoke access

5) Budget & Alert annotations in the export
   - If 'Include budgets' checked, append columns: budget_id, budget_name, budget_target, budget_window, budget_variance, budget_state (ok/over)
   - If 'Include alerts' checked, append: alert_id, alert_name, alert_severity, alert_trigger_value, alert_timestamp
   - For both include a small provenance section at the bottom of CSV: "Budget definitions snapshot v{schema_version} at {timestamp}"

Edge cases, constraints, and privacy notes:
- Always respect RBAC: if a user lacks visibility to a cost center, that row must be excluded server-side (not just hidden client-side).
- Large orgs: exports may exceed memory; enforce async pipeline with chunked exports.
- PII: strip personal emails from exported 'requestor' fields unless user opts in (enterprise). Store hashed requestor id for audit.
- Retention: export history visible for 180 days by default; enterprise can configure retention.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Single "Export & Downloads" modal available to users with billing view permission.
- Quick Export: default last invoice CSV includes allocation and budget columns when toggled. Sync download for <=50k rows.
- Async flow queues exports >50k rows, shows status in Export History, and delivers via email/S3.
- Export payload contains minimal provenance fields (export_id, requested_by, timestamp, schema_version).

Grooming backlog (prioritized):
1) Implement modal shell + Quick Export presets (2 wks) - P0
2) Server API: sync CSV for small ranges + column set (3 wks) - P0
3) Async export worker + email delivery (4 wks) - P0
4) Export History UI + RBAC enforcement tests (2 wks) - P1
5) Budget & Alerts inclusion toggles + schema versioning (3 wks) - P1
6) Share links + expiry/revoke controls (2 wks) - P2
7) S3 direct delivery + enterprise retention settings (4 wks) - P2
8) Audit-signed exports (PGP signing) for regulated customers (TBD legal/compliance) - P3

Dependencies & risks:
- Backend: need aggregation endpoint that merges allocation rules with charge data (ENG-exports epic).
- Compliance: verify PII handling and signed export requirements for auditors (Legal sign-off required).
- Infra: S3 credentials + ephemeral links for enterprise deliveries.
- UX: design token table for CSV column defaults (see Figma link).

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes-to-self):
- Should budgets included in exports capture historical budget definitions (snapshot) or reference latest live config? Snapshot preferred for auditability but heavier.
- How to present allocation rules in CSV so they are reproducible? Proposal: include rule_id and human-readable expression.
- Row-level RBAC vs column redaction: safer to exclude rows server-side, but may frustrate users expecting blanks. Document behavior clearly.
- CSV vs Parquet: Parquet better for big data but less friendly for immediate human review. Offer both.

Quick mockup checklist for design handoff:
- Modal: accessible keyboard nav, aria labels for tabs, compact defaults for quick export.
- Export History: sortable by date, filter by requester, status badges (queued/processing/failed/complete).
- Toasts & notifications: immediate feedback on queueing and finished exports, include direct download CTA.

Next steps (this week):
- Sync with ENG exports lead (Jira: EXPORTS-ownership-matrix) to confirm API contract and row limit for sync downloads (Marcus to schedule).
- UX: create two quick wireframes for Quick Export vs Custom Export (Evelyn to draft in Figma by 2024-10-18).
- Compliance: draft PII handling note and circulate to Legal (Priya to own).
- Add unit tests for RBAC enforcement in export API (Diego to prototype).

Notes / running log (choppy brainstorming bits):
- "include budget snapshots" flagged by Legal for retention implications
- "50k rows seems reasonable for sync" — sounds arbitrary, validate with infra memory perf tests
- Remember to surface the model name mapping (internally we map model_id -> model_handle) so exports are human readable
- Slack threads: #billing-ux, #platform-exports

References & context links (copy these into PR):
- Figma: See linked_artifacts above for mockups.
- Existing billing exports: CONFLUENCE-4567 (wip)
- Infra tickets: EXPORTS-queue-009, EXPORTS-chunking-012

Owner notes: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and contains open questions. Draft is ready for product review; after alignment we'll break the backlog into smaller tickets with acceptance criteria attached.

---- end of playbook draft ----
